fact_text: Flat steel is the sheet category of steel, sold as hot-rolled coil (HRC), cold-rolled coil (CRC), galvanised and colour-coated sheet, as distinct from rebar and girders.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Flat steel demand comes mainly from motorcycle and auto parts, with further use in appliances such as fridges and freezers, transformers and storage boxes, so it tracks consumer and industrial demand more than construction.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Flat steel production is far less energy intensive than long steel such as rebar, which makes electricity a much smaller cost driver for flat steel makers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the flat steel process, hot-rolled coil is pickled to remove its oxide layer, preheated to about 80 to 100 degrees Celsius to drive off moisture without melting, then cold-rolled at room temperature into thinner, smoother CRC.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Galvanised steel is made by dipping CRC in molten zinc to add a rust-protecting layer, and colour-coated steel is galvanised sheet with primer and paint applied on top.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Hot-rolled coil is the main raw material for flat steel makers and makes up roughly 70 to 80% of overall production cost.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Flat steel profitability depends mainly on the price spread between HRC and the finished product (CRC, galvanised or colour-coated), so a narrowing spread tightens margins directly.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Producing one tonne of CRC uses about 100 units of electricity, so power is a significant part of the conversion cost, which also covers distribution and administrative costs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Flat steel is mostly sold for cash, so its working capital cycle is much shorter than long steel, where dealers typically pay two to three months after delivery.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A flat steel maker typically holds about one month of raw material inventory as a buffer, so its invested capital includes working capital, not just the plant cost.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The roughly 30% import duty on CRC gives local makers a protection buffer that grows with the CRC price: about $240 per tonne at $800 CRC versus about $120 at $400.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Exports get no duty protection, so under normal conditions a flat steel maker earns roughly $20 per tonne on exports versus up to around $100 per tonne on local sales.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When flat steel volumes rise, check whether the growth comes from local sales or exports, because local sales carry far higher profit per tonne because of duty protection.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A flat steel company's return can be estimated by taking volume times the HRC-to-product spread for gross profit, then deducting finance, distribution and admin costs to reach profit before tax, and tax to reach net profit.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In FY25, importers captured an estimated 50 to 60% of the local flat steel market through misdeclared imports and exemptions, and that share is slowly returning to local producers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The National Tariff Commission imposed tariffs of up to 40% on Galvalume imports from certain countries, curbing a practice where importers dumped cheap Galvalume into Pakistan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Galvalume is a steel coated with a mix of zinc and aluminium, which resists rust and corrosion better and lasts longer than standard galvanised steel.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Steel firms registered in the FATA and PATA regions had been exempt from 18% sales tax and income tax, letting them undercut other cities; that exemption is being phased out, with a 10% sales tax rising 2% a year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The FATA and PATA phase-out is expected to create a level playing field for documented steel makers in about four years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: If import duties on finished flat steel fall through tariff rationalisation, which the IMF is pushing for, landed import costs drop, competition rises and local makers must cut prices, squeezing margins.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The Competition Commission of Pakistan found ISL part of a flat steel cartel that ran from July 2020 to December 2023 and fined it; the company says it will review the decision and may challenge it in court.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The Competition Commission of Pakistan fined Aisha Steel Mills for the flat steel cartel that ran from July 2020 to December 2023; the company plans to review the decision and take legal steps.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The cartel found by the Competition Commission was said to have inflated flat steel prices by up to 111%; such regulatory findings are often contested in court, so the final outcome is uncertain.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: ISL is described as one of the two largest flat steel makers in Pakistan, with a total capacity of about 1 million tonnes across CRC, galvanised and colour-coated products.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: ISL uses a mix of captive gas-fired power, solar and grid electricity; a captive gas levy and industrial power tariff changes decide whether it leans on grid power, and the analyst expected more grid use going forward.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In a scenario built on assumptions, ISL sells about 420,000 tonnes of flat steel in FY26, and the analyst's gross-profit estimates depend on the HRC-CRC spread and pricing assumptions.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Aisha Steel Mills is a major Karachi-based flat steel maker, part of the Arif Habib group, with total capacity of roughly 700,000 tonnes across CRC, galvanised and colour-coated products.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Aisha Steel Mills' sales volumes rose from about 20,000 tonnes to about 43,000 tonnes in Q1 FY26, a sign that flat steel demand is recovering and that volume is moving back to documented producers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Aisha Steel Mills carries a heavy debt burden because weak steel demand and high interest rates in earlier years pushed its annual finance cost up, which weighs on profit before tax.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In an assumption-based scenario, Aisha Steel Mills' flat steel sales volume could rise in FY27 toward roughly 200,000 tonnes, with profit estimates depending on pricing and policy.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Karachi-based flat steel makers can serve local demand and export to the USA, Europe and Canada through the port without extra freight cost.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues that PSX entry points after an oil-shock market correction have historically produced good returns over the following years, though no outcome is guaranteed.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'Inside Pakistan’s Flat Steel Industry. ISL & Aisha Steel Analysis.' (YouTube transcript, undated)
